property_summary: supportsInterface must return true for the IERC1155 interface ID in the reference contract, but the mutant erroneously returns false because it checks against IERC165 instead.

The original contract reports support for both IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI via supportsInterface, while the mutant replaces IERC1155 with IERC165 and thus breaks support for the IERC1155 interface.
The reference contract's supportsInterface must return true for the IERC1155 interface ID, while the mutant returns false because it checks for IERC165 instead.

For any valid ERC1155 interface identifier, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns the same as its super implementation for all other IDs, but the mutant incorrectly returns true for the IERC165 ID while the reference does not.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true iff the interfaceId equals type(IERC1155).interfaceId, type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId, or is supported by the parent ERC165/ERC1155; the mutant breaks this by returning true for type(IERC165).interfaceId instead of type(IERC1155).interfaceId.
supportsInterface must return true for IERC1155MetadataURI; the bug incorrectly returns false for it, breaking ERC1155 interface identification.

The supportsInterface function should return true for all interfaces it truly supports, but the buggy version returns false for ERC165 due to replacing the super call with false, breaking ERC165 compliance.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the buggy version returns false for that input.

For any interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI, then it must also return true for IERC165; the bug breaks this because it never returns true for IERC165, disconnected from the IERC1155 results.

For any interfaceId, if supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true then it must also return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the buggy version breaks this by returning true for IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI while returning false for IERC165.
The correct supportsInterface returns true for either IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI, while the mutant uses AND and thus returns false for either interface individually.
For any interfaceId that is exactly one of IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI, the correct contract returns true, while the mutant incorrectly returns false due to the AND instead of OR.

In the reference contract C, balanceOf for a non-zero address always returns the actual token balance minted or transferred to that account. The buggy version returns 0, breaking the invariant that after minting tokens to an account, balanceOf reflects the minted amount.
For any account that has been minted tokens, balanceOf(account, tokenId) must return the minted amount; the buggy version always returns 0, violating this invariant.
After minting tokens to a non-zero address, balanceOf must return at least the minted amount; the bug returns 0, violating this.
For any token minted to a non-zero address, the balanceOf query must return a value greater than zero; the bug causes it to return exactly 0.
For any non-zero address that has received a mint (balance was increased via _mint), the balanceOf query must return a value strictly greater than 0; the bug returns 0.
For any valid input arrays of equal length, calling c.balanceOfBatch(accounts, ids) should never revert, but the mutant may revert due to an out-of-bounds array access when i == accounts.length.

For any equal-length address and uint256 arrays, the reference balanceOfBatch returns an array of the same length containing correct balances, while the buggy version reverts or returns incorrect data due to an out-of-bounds access when i equals accounts.length.

For any admissible equal-length input arrays, the reference balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals the input length, while the mutant reads out-of-bounds causing either a revert or returned array of different length.

For any equal-length input arrays, the reference balanceOfBatch returns an array of the same length without reverting, while the mutant can revert due to an out-of-bounds access when i equals accounts.length.

For any admissible equal-length input arrays, the reference balanceOfBatch returns a uint256[] of the same length, and the buggy version either reverts or returns a differently-length array due to reading past the array bounds.
